context: systems-integration- & safety-certification-led · elevated guideway fronts the programme

brief.intro: A monorail or automated people mover (APM) is a driverless transit system running on an elevated (or sometimes at-grade) guideway between stations, controlled entirely by signalling and automatic train control rather than a driver. The programme has two very different halves: first, a civil job — piers, guideway beams and stations — that behaves like a linear infrastructure project; second, a systems-integration job — traction power, signalling/ATC, vehicles and platform screen doors — that behaves like commissioning one complex machine spread across the whole line. Guideway civils have to be substantially complete early because the systems contractor needs a finished, surveyed structure to install rail, power and signalling equipment on. From that point, the schedule is owned by dynamic testing and the safety-certification process, which a regulator paces, not the contractor.

must_get_right: Guideway civils are the enabler, not the driver — hand over a surveyed, dimensionally accurate structure early so the systems contractor can install rail, power and signalling without waiting on construction.

Signalling/ATC integration is the true critical path — it takes longer and carries more risk than the civil works, and it cannot start meaningfully until traction power and a continuous stretch of guideway are ready.
Protect the dynamic-testing and safety-certification window — the regulator sets the pace here, not the contractor, and re-test loops are common; build in real float, not optimistic overlap.
Vehicles are long-lead and system-specific — order early and align their delivery and static testing with when the guideway and power are actually ready to receive them.

basis_of_planning.standard: AACE Recommended Practice 38R-06 — Documenting the Schedule Basis

sections.heading: Scheduling method & tools
sections.body: A Critical Path Method (CPM) network built in Primavera P6, developed to a Level 3 control schedule with retained-logic progress. Activities carry durations in working days; the network is calculated (F9) with no artificial constraints beyond contractual milestones. Total float is kept ≥ 0 in the baseline.

sections.heading: Calendars & working time
sections.body: Guideway civils run a 6-day week with night-time possessions where the alignment crosses live roads or rail; signalling and systems integration move to a 7-day calendar at peak to compress the testing window; dynamic testing follows the regulator's approved test calendar, often night-only in early stages.

sections.heading: Sequencing logic & critical path
sections.body: The driving path runs guideway civils (piers → beams) → traction power & third-rail install → signalling/ATC trackside install & configuration → vehicle delivery & static test → dynamic testing → trial running → safety certification. Stations are not on the critical path once the guideway they connect to is structurally complete.

sections.heading: Key assumptions
sections.body: Alignment and station locations are fixed before pier foundations start; the systems design (traction power, signalling) is frozen before trackside install; a single vehicle-delivery campaign; regulatory review runs in parallel with, not after, dynamic testing where the authority permits it.

sections.heading: Access, resource & site constraints
sections.body: Guideway erection needs crane/launching-gantry windows and, over live roads or rail, possession windows; systems integration needs exclusive, protected access to the guideway; dynamic-testing and safety-certification specialists are a scarce, shared resource that gates the back end of the programme.

sections.heading: Risks, float & contingency
sections.body: Principal risks: beam-erection possession slippage, signalling/ATC integration rework, and safety-certification re-submission cycles. Contingency is held before dynamic testing and before certification submission rather than spread across civil activities.

sections.heading: Schedule levels of detail
sections.body: Reported at Level 1 (milestones) and Level 2 (summary) to the client; controlled at Level 3; expanded to Level 4–5 lookahead for the field — consistent with AACE 37R-06.
